transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. Yeah, um, thanks for seeing me. So, I guess what finally scared me into actually coming in—because I've been putting this off for a while, honestly, just hoping it would get better on its own—is that work is just getting really, really stressful because of these mistakes I'm making. 

I'm a camera operator and a video editor, which means there are a million little moving parts and files to manage all the time. I've been doing this for a long time, I have my degree in it, but I just keep making these incredibly dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. Like, I'll be on set and I'll label the camera cards completely wrong before handing them off, which causes a huge headache for the whole post-production team, or I'll be in the editing bay and just completely miss a timecode note that a director explicitly gave me. 

And the worst part, the thing that really made me pick up the phone and make this appointment, was the other day when I exported a client cut—like, a final version meant for review—with the completely wrong lower-third graphic on the screen. And I had checked it! I literally sat there, reviewed the timeline, told myself it was good to go, and I still somehow missed it. It's just so frustrating and embarrassing because I know how to do my job, but it's like my brain just skips over these crucial little details no matter how hard I try to lock in, and I'm terrified I'm going to ruin my reputation or get fired if I don't figure out why I keep doing this.
Have you had trouble with attention, distractibility, or careless mistakes since childhood?

Oh, gosh, yeah. Um... it’s actually kind of a running joke in my family, though honestly it wasn’t very funny to me at the time. If you look at my old report cards—my mom kept all of them in this big plastic storage bin in her attic, and we actually went through them a few years ago—it’s just note after note from my teachers about my behavior. 

Even way back in elementary school, like first, second, third grade, my teachers were constantly having to move my desk. They’d put me right up front by the chalkboard, or sometimes completely separated from the rest of the kids. You know how they used to group desks together in those little clusters or pods? Yeah, I wasn't allowed in the pods. Because I was just... I was always out of my seat. I literally couldn't just sit there. I'd be up sharpening my pencil for the fifth time or just wandering over to the reading corner because I felt like it. 

And the talking, oh my gosh. I was always blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. I just couldn't hold it in, it felt like the answer was just going to explode out of my mouth. Or I'd be bothering my classmates, like leaning over and talking to them while we were supposed to be doing quiet work, or tapping on their desks, and the crazy thing is, I swear I wouldn't even realize I was doing it until the teacher snapped my name. I'd just be acting, and then suddenly the teacher is saying, "Sit down and be quiet!" and I'd be like, "Wait, what?" It was just like my body was doing things before my brain could catch up and stop it. 

So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing. It's just... it's manifesting differently now that I'm an adult trying to hold down a professional job, you know? Back then it was just, "Oh, she's a handful, she has too much energy," but now it's my actual livelihood on the line.
